item.text: I found the DOL ETA claims archive page and the current DOL claims PDF. The PDF has a same-variant table of seasonally adjusted U.S. initial claims in thousands through week ending September 5, 2026; the archive page gives the weekly Thursday 8:30 a.m. release policy and the 2026 holiday exception list.

There is a target-calendar inconsistency: the registered window ends on October 8, 2026, while the DOL weekly claims release policy would normally put the first print for week ending September 19, 2026 on Thursday, September 24, 2026. I’ll keep the forecast tied to the registered target and disclose that discrepancy in the reasoning.

item.text: I’ve got enough source context. I’m just calculating the interval from the fetched same-series DOL table now, using recent successive changes in the seasonally adjusted initial claims series.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
import statistics as st
vals=[230,227,216,217,217,209,189,198,200,212,207,204,207,206]
chg=[b-a for a,b in zip(vals, vals[1:])]
print(chg)
print('n',len(chg),'mean',sum(chg)/len(chg),'sample_stdev',st.stdev(chg),'pop_stdev',st.pstdev(chg),'half',1.28*st.stdev(chg))
print('last4avg',sum(vals[-4:])/4, 'last6avg',sum(vals[-6:])/6)
PY"
